children.description: Procumbent herb with perennial root, root ca. 4 mm in diam; shape and size of bladder cells unknown. children.name: Ruschia variabilis Klak, 2023
children.description: 3.1.8. Conservation status Plants were found in a restricted area (Fig. 4) on low hills close to the sea, which are characterized by a cooler climate than areas further inland and away from the sea. In addition, the substrate where it occurs differs from the sandy coastal habitat surrounding these low hills. As we consider the habitat preference of this species to be rather specific, we suggest a status of vulnerable (VU) for this species.

children.name: Drosanthemopsis bella Klak
children.description: Distribution and ecology: Drosanthemopsis bella is known from a single population near Garies in southern Namaqualand (Map 6). The plants grow in heavy loam over weathered shales in otherwise almost bare patches of quartz-gravel. Flowering takes place between August and September.

children.name: Drosanthemopsis kwaganapensis Klak
children.description: Conservation status: The species is known from two quartz patches between Port Nolloth and Grootmis. At both localities about 20 plants were seen. We propose an IUCN category of vulnerable (VU) in line with that for D. vaginata.

children.name: Drosanthemopsis diversifolia
children.description: Ecology and distribution: The species prefers deep loamy soils, with or without a thin cover of quartz gravel, in areas with winter rain, mean annual precipitation <125 mm. Flowering between July and September. The species is common in the Vanrhynsdorp and Vredendal districts and extends also to the north-east to the Calvinia district, where it is much rarer. Its most southern location is at the Doorn River Bridge, north of Clanwilliam (Fig. 6).
